Use cache-aside for read-heavy data, and set TTLs to control staleness. Read replicas (RDS, Aurora, Azure SQL, Cloud SQL) scale reads and can be promoted for DR, but replication is asynchronous, so expect some lag. Neither a cache nor a read replica scales writes.

Data residency means keeping data, and often its replicas and backups, inside an approved geography. You control it by choosing Regions, restricting replication targets, and enforcing allowed Regions with guardrails. Examples are SCPs in AWS Organizations, Azure Policy 'Allowed locations' and Google Cloud's resource locations organization policy constraint. Remember to check backups, global tables and CDN caches, because they can copy data across borders.

concepts.term: Online vs offline transfer and DMS
concepts.explanation: Online tools include AWS DataSync, Storage Transfer Service, AzCopy and Azure Storage Mover, often over Direct Connect, ExpressRoute or Cloud Interconnect. Offline devices include AWS Snowball Edge, Azure Data Box and Google Transfer Appliance; use them when the network would take too long. For databases, AWS DMS, Azure Database Migration Service and Google Database Migration Service do a full load and then change data capture (CDC) for near-zero-downtime cutover. Heterogeneous moves, such as Oracle to PostgreSQL, also need schema conversion, for example DMS Schema Conversion or AWS SCT.

keyFacts: AWS S3 minimum storage durations: Standard-IA and One Zone-IA 30 days; Glacier Instant Retrieval 90 days; Glacier Flexible Retrieval 90 days; Glacier Deep Archive 180 days.
Glacier Deep Archive retrieval: Standard completes within 12 hours and Bulk within 48 hours; Glacier Instant Retrieval returns data in milliseconds.

Azure Blob tiers: Hot, Cool (30 days), Cold (90 days) and Archive (180 days). Archive is offline, so you must rehydrate a blob before reading it, which can take up to about 15 hours at standard priority.
Google Cloud Storage classes: Standard, Nearline (30 days), Coldline (90 days) and Archive (365 days). All classes have millisecond access, but colder classes charge retrieval fees.

S3 Standard-IA and Glacier Instant Retrieval bill a minimum object size of 128 KB. By default, S3 lifecycle does not transition objects smaller than 128 KB. Archived objects in Glacier Flexible Retrieval and Deep Archive also carry about 40 KB of per-object metadata overhead, so batch small log files before archiving.

Seven years is about 2,557 days, including leap days. Set expiration at or just after the legal retention period, and use Object Lock, an immutable policy or Bucket Lock if deletion must be prevented.
Transfer rule of thumb: 100 TB over a fully used 1 Gbps link takes about 9–10 days. If the online transfer would take more than about a week, or bandwidth is shared, consider an offline device.
Aurora keeps six copies of data across three AZs and supports up to 15 Aurora Replicas. Cosmos DB's default consistency is Session. Spanner multi-region instances have a 99.999% SLA.
Decision rule: use a cache to cut read latency, use read replicas to scale reads and support DR, and use sharding or a distributed database (DynamoDB, Cosmos DB, Spanner) to scale writes.

example.caption: S3 lifecycle for 200 TB of logs kept 7 years. Costs are approximate us-east-1 list prices; confirm in the AWS Pricing Calculator. Standard at about USD 0.023/GB-month × 204,800 GB ≈ USD 4,700/month. Deep Archive at about USD 0.00099/GB-month ≈ USD 200/month. Keep 30 days hot for troubleshooting, then archive. Enable Object Lock (compliance mode, 7 years) on the bucket for WORM.

pitfalls: Ignoring minimum storage durations. For example, moving data to Google Archive (365 days) or S3 Deep Archive (180 days) and then deleting or re-tiering it early still bills the full minimum.
Archiving millions of tiny log files. Per-object transition request charges and archive metadata overhead can exceed the storage savings, so compress and batch logs into larger objects first.

Treating lifecycle expiration as retention compliance. Expiration only deletes data; it does not stop early deletion. Exams expect Object Lock compliance mode, Azure immutable policies or Bucket Lock for WORM.

Choosing Azure Archive or S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval or Deep Archive when the scenario needs instant reads. Pick Glacier Instant Retrieval, Azure Cold or a Google Cloud class (all have millisecond access) instead.
Using read replicas or a cache to fix a write bottleneck. Replicas are asynchronous and scale reads only.
Forgetting that multi-region replicas, global tables and backups can break data residency rules.

workflow.title: Designing a log retention tier and lifecycle policy

steps.label: Capture retention and access needs
steps.detail: Record the retention period (7 years), whether WORM is mandatory, and how often and how fast old logs must be read.

steps.label: Size and shape the data
steps.detail: Estimate total volume, daily ingest and object count, then compress and batch small files into larger objects.

steps.label: Map access patterns to tiers
steps.detail: Keep recent logs in a hot tier for troubleshooting and push older logs to the cheapest archive tier the read SLA allows.

steps.label: Check minimum durations and fees
steps.detail: Confirm each transition happens after the previous tier's minimum duration and that retrieval and request fees fit the budget.

steps.label: Write the lifecycle policy
steps.detail: Define the transitions, expire objects at 2,557 days, delete noncurrent versions and abort incomplete multipart uploads.

steps.label: Enforce immutability and residency
steps.detail: Enable Object Lock, an immutable policy or Bucket Lock for 7 years, and restrict the bucket and its replicas to approved Regions.

steps.label: Estimate and monitor cost
steps.detail: Model the cost in the pricing calculator, then track actual spend with storage analytics and cost tools.

project.title: log-archive-7y

It uses Standard, then Glacier Instant Retrieval, then Deep Archive, with Object Lock (WORM) to enforce retention; Terraform builds the bucket, a Python script estimates per-tier storage with your own prices, and a second script verifies the retention rule.
